name: DLL3 (delta-like ligand 3)
summary: DLL3 is an inhibitory Notch ligand aberrantly expressed on the surface of most small-cell lung cancers and other high-grade neuroendocrine carcinomas, making it a target for T-cell engagers and other DLL3-directed therapies.
biology: DLL3 is a transcriptional target of ASCL1, the dominant lineage transcription factor in neuroendocrine SCLC. In normal cells DLL3 is mainly localised to the Golgi and inhibits Notch signalling in cis; in SCLC it is overexpressed and partly translocated to the cell surface, with minimal expression on normal adult tissues. Expression is highest in ASCL1-high (SCLC-A) tumours and lower in non-neuroendocrine subtypes.

testing.notes: DLL3 expression is not currently required to select patients for tarlatamab; the predictive value of DLL3 IHC remains under investigation.

predictiveRelevance: DLL3 is the target of tarlatamab, a DLL3xCD3 bispecific T-cell engager used in previously treated SCLC. Other DLL3-directed modalities (T-cell engagers, CAR-T cells, radioligands) are in development. The earlier DLL3-directed antibody-drug conjugate rovalpituzumab tesirine was discontinued.
resistance: Lineage plasticity towards non-neuroendocrine (e.g. YAP1/POU2F3-high) phenotypes with lower DLL3 expression
cnsConsiderations: SCLC frequently metastasises to the brain; the activity of DLL3-directed T-cell engagers in untreated brain metastases is not well characterised.
